profile.reading:
DataBank LAS1 sits at 7185 Pollock Drive, Las Vegas, Nevada, near the city's downtown Innovation District. DataBank's own facility page states 57,364 square feet of IT space and 3.35 megawatts of critical IT load, with a 2N power design and N+1 cooling supporting air-cooled racks up to 10 kilowatts and liquid-cooled racks up to 25 kilowatts per cabinet, 11 to 12 onsite network carriers, and SOC 1/2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 compliance certifications. DataBank does not name the power utility on LAS1's page; NV Energy is the dominant electric utility across the Las Vegas metro as a matter of public record, though this is not stated by DataBank directly. DataBank's marketing materials for the Las Vegas market cite the state's low sales taxes and absence of a state income tax as general business-climate advantages, without specifically naming or citing the terms of Nevada's data center sales-and-use-tax abatement program administered by the Governor's Office of Economic Development under state law, so that program's applicability to LAS1 specifically is not asserted here. DataBank does not state a year-opened date for LAS1, and it does not appear on the company's acquisition-history page, implying an organically built facility rather than one acquired from a prior operator, though this is inferred rather than stated. Las Vegas has grown as a secondary data center market over the past decade, drawing operators seeking lower land and power costs relative to coastal California markets while remaining within low-latency reach of Southern California.

Las Vegas has grown into a recognized secondary U.S. data center market over the past decade, with Switch's large SUPERNAP campuses and other colocation operators establishing a substantial regional presence alongside DataBank, drawn by lower land and power costs relative to coastal California, seismic stability, and low-latency reach into Southern California markets. Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development has periodically publicized the state's data center incentive framework as a tool for economic diversification beyond gaming and tourism, though the specific statutory terms of any abatement applicable to LAS1 are not confirmed in DataBank's own materials.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for Las Vegas, fetched this session, describes this facility as LAS1 and gives its address as 7185 Pollock Drive, Las Vegas, NV 89119, with 3.35 MW of critical IT load and 57,364 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank LAS1 in Las Vegas holds 3.35 MW of IT load across 57,364 square feet. At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, this suggests roughly 84 racks, or if IT load were divided between training and other workloads, potentially fewer accelerator clusters. The facility's published specifications do not note what workloads it hosts or certifications for GPU-intensive computing.

Nevada has mapped 26 data center facilities but only two with published power capacity on record. LAS1 ranks third among those two by published megawatts, and the state's total published capacity stands at 10.37 MW, a figure that reflects sparse public disclosure rather than installed capacity. This facility accounts for about one third of Nevada's published IT load.

The operator, DataBank, runs more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets and is majority-owned by Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest as of 2022. The company's capacity portfolio, scale, and operator status suggest it can provision for enterprise and cloud customers, but whether LAS1 itself is deployed for AI workloads or serves other segments is not published.
